briefdescription.para: Constructor for the reporter class.

detaileddescription.para:
argvs
Owning pointer to the command-line arguments vector; the reporter takes ownership via move.
Moves the supplied argument vector into argvs_ and scans it for the --verbose, --quiet, --silent, and --output-file options (the latter as --output-file=<path> or --output-file <path>), adjusting verbosity_ and optionally opening the output file. If the output file path is missing or the file cannot be opened, the process exits with a diagnostic error message. The internal string buffer is pre-allocated to reduce dynamic allocation overhead.

briefdescription.para: Virtual destructor for the reporter class.

detaileddescription.para: Virtual, so that the concrete reporters, owned through a pointer to this base class, are destroyed correctly.

If an output file was opened, it is flushed and closed, and a confirmation message naming the output file is written to stdout. If tracing is enabled, the function signature is output for diagnostic purposes.

briefdescription.para: Output operator to display any pointer.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The type of the pointer.
v
The pointer value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload enables the reporter to output pointer values in a consistent and readable format.
Null pointers are always rendered as the string "0x0", regardless of the platform, avoiding platform-specific representations such as "(nil)" on Linux/glibc.

Non-null pointers are formatted as a hexadecimal address using snprintf with the p format specifier. The resulting string is appended to the internal output buffer, allowing pointer values to be included in test reports and diagnostics.
This approach provides clear and unambiguous representation of pointer addresses, which is particularly useful for debugging and verifying pointer-related test cases.

Reference to the current reporter instance.
This template operator overload allows the reporter to output values of any arithmetic type (integral or floating-point) in a consistent and readable format. The value is formatted using the detail::append_number_() helper, without a type suffix (unlike the detail::expression_formatter operators, which add one).

briefdescription.para: Output the current buffered content to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: The buffer is written without appending a line ending, and is not cleared. ANSI colour sequences are removed, so the file receives plain text even when the console output is coloured. If no output file is open, the call has no effect.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Writes the contents of buffer_ to output_file_ without appending a newline. If output_file_ is null, the call is a no-op.

The buffer may contain ANSI colour sequences, added when the console is a terminal, which must not reach the file. They are removed while writing: each ESC [, followed by any digits and semicolons, and terminated by m, is skipped, and the text between the sequences is written unchanged. Any other use of ESC is written as is.

briefdescription.para: Write formatted text to the console.

detaileddescription.para: All reporter console output is routed through this function, so that it reaches the standard output stream via a single path, shared with the output of the user printf() calls. Using one stream-based path keeps the reporter and user output in the same buffer, preserving their relative order.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on stdout. The stream is explicit, so the compiler does not rewrite the call into puts() or putchar(), and all console output shares the same FILE-based path.

briefdescription.para: Write formatted text to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: If no output file is open, the call has no effect, so callers do not need to check output_file_ themselves.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on output_file_. If output_file_ is null, the arguments are ignored.

briefdescription.para: Writes the informational (non-result) lines to the console and to the output file.

detaileddescription.para:
Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Constructs and emits two informational lines, each prefixed by get_comment_prefix(): the first lists the program name (without the path) and any command-line arguments; the second identifies the compiler (Clang, GCC, or MSVC) together with the version string, floating-point availability on bare-metal targets, exception support, and any active debug or trace macros. Both lines are written to the output file when one is open, and to stdout when the verbosity is normal or verbose, except when both MICRO_OS_PLUS_STARTUP_ENABLED and MICRO_OS_PLUS_DIAG_TRACE_ENABLED are defined, since the startup code already displays this information.

briefdescription.para: Abstract base class for the reporters that display test results, including operand values for failures.

detaileddescription.para: The reporter class is responsible for presenting test results within the µTest++ framework. It accumulates output in a buffer, using basic output operators for strings, characters, booleans, numbers, and pointers, and writes it to the console and to an optional output file.

For failed checks, the reporter prints the actual values of the operands, pre-formatted by its detail::expression_formatter (with type suffixes for numbers), supporting precise diagnostics and efficient debugging. The class supports multiple verbosity levels and colour-coded output to distinguish between successful and failed checks.

The pure virtual methods report the beginning and end of the session, the suites, and the subtests, and format the pass and fail results; they are implemented by reporter_human and reporter_tap. The concrete reporter is created by the runner, as selected by the --reporter command-line option.
All members and methods are defined within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.
